newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bell still eyes Romania planemaker.
newsitem.headline: Bell still eyes Romania planemaker.

text.p: Bell Helicopter Textron has reiterated plans to buy a stake in a Romanian helicopter maker and build helicopters in Romania, the government said on Tuesday.
"Bell Helicopter reasserted its proposal in principle regarding its intention to buy a share package in IAR in (the Transylvanian city of) Brasov," a government statement said.
It said Bell Helicopter's plan was reaffirmed when Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea met the company's president Lloyd Shoppa in Bucharest on Monday.
The statement also said Shoppa was accompanied by Louis Bevilaqua of General Electric. The U.S. company intended to buy a stake in Bucharest's Turbomecanica SA aircraft engine maker, it said.

Bell Helicopter signed a memorandum last September to start production of 96 Cobra attack helicopters at state-run Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana SA (IAR) after buying 51 percent in the company from its majority stockholder the State Ownership Fund.

If the deal goes through, IAR would produce twin-engined AH-1W Super Cobra attack helicopters under licence, with Bell supplying technology and training. It would also establish Textron's first manufacturing presence in Eastern Europe.
IAR would make the airframe, while Turbomecanica would produce engines.
IAR already has a deal with Eurocopter, a joint venture of France's Aerospatiale and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, to build 80 small Ecureuil helicopters.
